sections.h2: Where do Mercer County deeds get recorded, and what are the office hours?
sections.html:
The Mercer County Recorder of Deeds works from Suite 109 of the courthouse complex at 125 S. Diamond Street in the borough of Mercer, the county seat. The phone number is 724-662-3800, and the counter keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 4:30, holidays excepted.

The same counter takes deeds, mortgages, leases, powers of attorney, easements, subdivision plans and notary bonds. For a house sale the order is simple: the deed is signed at closing, a Uniform Parcel Identifier is certified, and the closing agent files the deed with the transfer tax and the fee. The county's fee bill also says recordings can be checked online through the Land Records Search on the county website, with the index and images going back to 1972.

Mercer County covers 673 square miles of land in northwest Pennsylvania along the Ohio line, and its largest city is Hermitage. Sellers in Sharon, Grove City, Greenville or Farrell all record through this one office.

School district names matter on a deed because local transfer tax can be shared with the district. Mercer County is served by Commodore Perry, Farrell Area, Greenville Area, Grove City Area, Hermitage, Jamestown Area, Lakeview, Mercer Area, Reynolds, Sharon City, Sharpsville Area, West Middlesex Area and Wilmington Area, so the property description should place the parcel in the right municipality and district. Interstates 79, 80 and 376 and US routes 19 and 62 cross the county.

sections.h2: What changed with the UPI ordinance in Mercer County in 2026?
sections.html:
Mercer County certifies a Uniform Parcel Identifier for every document that affects title before it can be recorded. The commissioners passed Ordinance No. 2026-001 on November 20, 2025, and it took effect on January 5, 2026.

The UPI is simply the county tax parcel number already assigned to the property. The Tax Assessment Office certifies it, and a document mailed or e-recorded to the Recorder is forwarded there first, so the identifier is settled before the deed reaches the Recorder's desk.

  • The charge is $20.00 for each UPI certification, paid separately to Mercer County Tax Assessment, not to the Recorder.
  • Including the parent parcel number costs nothing extra.
  • When only part of a property is being conveyed, two UPI numbers are needed: one for the new piece and one for the parent parcel.
  • Deeds, quitclaim deeds, mortgages, releases, easements, leases, court decrees and powers of attorney to sell are all covered.
  • Questions and pre-approval requests go to upi@mercercountypa.gov.

An agent who wants the closing on schedule should send the draft deed to the Assessment Office well before the signing date.

sections.h2: How much does Mercer County charge to put a deed on record?
sections.html:
A deed costs $71.25 under the fee bill revised June 15, 2026. That base fee includes four pages, four names and one parcel, and the county adds $2.00 for each extra page and $0.50 for each extra parcel or name.

Mercer County Recorder of Deeds fee bill, revised June 15, 2026
Document or itemFee
Deed, including corrective deed and decree of distribution$71.25
Mortgage, including amendments and subordinations$71.25
Mortgage assignment, release, satisfaction$59.75
Easement or right of way agreement$71.25
Power of attorney$18.50
Realty transfer tax Statement of Value$2.00 extra
Copies made by staff$0.50 per page
Return of a rejected document$5.00 first time, $10 second, $20 after

Source: Mercer County Recorder of Deeds fee bill. The Statement of Value is not part of the four-page base fee, and the county asks for the original plus one copy.

Payment is by cash or check only, and each check needs the account holder's current address and phone number. A stamped return envelope lets the recorded deed travel back to the right buyer.

sections.h2: How much realty transfer tax applies in Mercer County towns?
sections.html:
The baseline is 1 percent to the Commonwealth plus 1 percent local, which the fee bill describes, and five places charge a different local rate. The recorder collects the whole amount when the deed is filed.

  • Hermitage: 2.5 percent local
  • Sharon: 2.5 percent local
  • Farrell: 2 percent local
  • Greenville: 2 percent local
  • Sheakleyville: 1 percent local, effective May 1, 2019

A deed that covers land in more than one municipality has to state how the transfer tax is divided or what percentage goes to each. The fee bill also prints a common level ratio factor of 9.52 for the period July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and under state revenue rules the grantor and grantee both stand behind the tax. Some family transfers, deeds to government bodies and inherited property are exempt from the state tax.

sections.h2: What document standards does the Mercer County Recorder enforce?
sections.html:
The office rejects paper that does not meet its standards, and a rejected document costs the return fee shown in the table. Sellers can avoid that by checking the deed against the county's list before closing.

  • Original documents only, with an acknowledgment date that does not come before the date of the document.
  • A 2-inch blank margin at the top of every page for the Recorder's stamp.
  • The municipality, county and state of the property written on deeds and mortgages.
  • A signed certificate of residence on deeds, mortgages, articles of agreement and assignments.
  • No highlighting, and text legible enough to index and copy.
  • When several documents belong to one transaction, a note on each showing the order of recording.

The county also requires either the transfer tax or a fully completed Statement of Value, using the current Pennsylvania form.

sections.h2: How does the Mercer County reassessment affect a house sale?
sections.html:
The last countywide reassessment finished in 1971, and the project to replace those values has slipped by a year. New assessed values take effect for the 2028 tax year instead of 2027, and in 2027 each owner will receive a Final Value Mailer showing land, improvements and the total.

By design, a reassessment does not raise total tax revenue. The county explains that the county, municipalities and school districts are to bill the same total after the change, so millage drops where values rise. In other counties, about a third of owners saw taxes fall, a third saw no change and a third saw an increase. A seller in Mercer County can tell a buyer that the value is likely to be reset soon and that the bill may move in either direction.

Once the mailer arrives, an owner can appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals, and the county code requires formal appeals to be finished by October 31 of the appeal year. For the current tax picture on a parcel, the Assessment Office at 724-662-7551 and the county's GIS parcel viewer show the county, municipal and school bills separately.

faqs.q: How much is the Mercer County UPI certification fee?
faqs.a: It is $20.00 for each UPI certification, paid to Mercer County Tax Assessment rather than to the Recorder. Naming the parent parcel on a document carries no extra fee.

faqs.q: What is the base price of a Mercer County deed filing?
faqs.a: A deed starts at $71.25, which pays for four pages, four names and one parcel. Each added page runs $2.00, each added name or parcel $0.50, and the Statement of Value tacks on $2.00.

faqs.q: Can Mercer County recording fees go on a credit card?
faqs.a: The county's document standards list cash or checks only. A check should show the account holder's current address and phone number.

faqs.q: Why is Hermitage transfer tax higher than the rest of Mercer County?
faqs.a: The fee bill lists Hermitage and Sharon at 2.5 percent local tax, while Farrell and Greenville charge 2 percent. Other places use the usual 1 percent local share on top of the 1 percent state tax.

faqs.q: When do new Mercer County property values take effect?
faqs.a: The county moved the reassessment to the 2028 tax year. Owners will get a Final Value Mailer in 2027 explaining the new values and how to appeal.
